newsitem.title: USA: CBOT old crop rice soars on export business.
newsitem.headline: CBOT old crop rice soars on export business.

text.p: CBOT rice futures posted double-digit gains for the second straight day on reports Costa Rica had purchased U.S. rice, pit sources said.
"The Costa Rica deal is for prompt shipment and they have indicated U.S. origin," a floor source said, referring to news Costa Rica bought 26,500 tonnes for June30-July 7 shipment.
The deal threatened to strain already tight U.S. old crop supplies. Floor sources said they expected commercials to cancel warehouse receipts to cover the business.
"The cash market for high grade rice is significantly higher than this market," another source said.
Concerns were also mounting about new crop conditions. Some floor sources said emergence was slow due to crusting soils. Slow development could lead to slow harvest, they said.
"The remaining supplies to bridge us between old crop and new crop are a lot less than what we anticipated," a pit source said. "That makes the timing of harvest that much more important."
Rice ended 19 to two cents per cwt higher with July up 15 at $11.73. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 800 lots, against Monday's actual volume of 918.
